title: docs(types): name the arbiter of `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` in its own header (objectui#9546)
body:
Fixes #9546

Names the arbiter of `packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` in the
file's own header. Option 1 of the three the card listed, ruled by the PM seat as a
verification-strategy / gate-blind-spot repair.

## The defect, exactly as narrow as the card stated it

The file is a TYPE-LEVEL ratchet judged by `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, while wearing
the extension of the command that does **not** judge it. It is not that vitest is
wrong, and not that the assertions are wrong — it is that the file never said which
command judges it. That is all this PR repairs. No assertion, ledger, fixture or
mirror is touched.

## Re-measured on this branch, not inherited

Every figure the card carried was re-derived on today's tree before the header
sentence was written, because the sentence is only true if the ablation still
reproduces.

| the card's claim | re-derived here | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| runtime `expect()` calls: 53 | 53 | reproduces |
| type-level assertion lines: 72 | 72 | reproduces |
| `tsconfig.test.json` includes the file | `"include": ["src/**/*.test.ts", "src/**/*.test.tsx"]` | reproduces |
| ablation: vitest exit 0 / tsc exit 2, `TS2322` | vitest **0**, tsc **2**, `TS2322` | reproduces |
| the file is 4519 lines | **4629** before this PR | MOVED — see below |

The 72 is a LINE count, reproduced with the card's own method (lines matching any of
the three type-level spellings). Counted as distinct assertion SITES it is smaller,
because that method also catches the two helper type definitions and the conditional
tails inside type helpers. Both readings are honest; they answer different questions.
The header this PR adds writes down **neither**, per AGENTS.md #9.

### The ablation, both ways on one tree

Mutation: `.omit({ body: true, children: true })` appended to
`data-display.zod.ts#StatisticSchema` — a registered pair — removing both content
channels from the mirror while the declaration still declares them.

- `vitest` on the violated tree: **exit 0**, `Test Files 1 passed (1)` /
  `Tests 32 passed (32)` — byte-identical to the summary line of the clean run. The
  runtime half does not merely pass; its output does not move at all.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` on the **identical** tree: **exit 2**, one
  `error TS2322`, firing at the `assertionUnmirroredMatchesLedger` declaration.

Green at rest was established first, both ways, so the exit code is a usable signal.
The mutation was proved to reach disk before either leg ran (injected-marker count
plus a blob-hash change), and the restore leg is proved byte-identical to the HEAD
blob with `git diff HEAD` empty. The ablation script carries a `trap` restoring from
`HEAD` by absolute path. Both halves resolve through relative source imports, so no
`dist/` is involved and no rebuild sits between the mutation and either instrument.

## Why a header sentence can carry it

The ruling hung on this and asked me to stop if it failed. It holds: the file is
hand-maintained and not generated, its header is an ordinary source docblock that is
never stripped, and the runtime half compiles and passes today. No fork to report.

## The wording is borrowed, not invented

`report-schema-authoring-face.test.ts`, in the same directory, already carries this
exact habit under the heading "Which instrument checks which assertion (stated,
because they differ)". This PR reuses that heading verbatim and follows its two-
paragraph shape. A convention beats a better sentence.

Two repo rules shaped the text: AGENTS.md #9 — it points at the instruments and
writes down none of their answers, so nothing in it can rot into a stale figure; and
AGENTS.md #11 — `tsconfig.test.json` is cited by name and by the content of its
`include`, never by a line address.

The closing clause is marked as a RECORD of a measurement and the guidance above it
as LIVE, which is this file's own governing split.

## Gates

`dispatch-gates.mjs` lives in the sister repo and REFUSES for objectui paths
(re-confirmed this run: exit 2, "asked for objectstack-ai/objectui, but this checkout
is objectstack-ai/objectstack"). The list below is therefore hand-derived from
objectui's own `package.json` scripts and `.github/workflows/`, and every exit code
was captured on its own line after a redirect, never through a pipe.

| gate | exit |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` (all three legs; the arbiter itself) | 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types test` — 191 files, 4530 tests | 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types lint` | 0 |
| `check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 |
| `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` / `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` / `check-changeset-claims.mjs` | 0 |
| `check-control-bytes.mjs` | 0 |
| `check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` | 0 |
| `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` | 0 — NOT GOVERNED |
| `check-test-path-roots.mjs` | 0 |

The type-check, control-bytes, line-citation and changeset gates were re-run at the
final commit `b0a2320`, after the last edit, so no gate reading predates the tree it
describes.

**Lint narrowing, declared.** The repo-wide `eslint .` is CI's run, not this PR's.
The narrowed run is the package's own `lint` script, which is the unit `turbo run
lint` invokes. Three readings, so the narrowing is a measurement rather than a gate
that merely did not run: the population is 262 files, read from eslint's own
resolution of its config, not guessed; the count comes from `--format json` output
length; and `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting — no `project` or
`projectService` key — so a comment-only edit in one file cannot move the verdict on
any untouched file. The changed file alone lints at 0 errors, 0 warnings. The 289
warnings in the package total are the pre-existing `no-explicit-any` baseline and are
untouched by this PR, which adds no code.

## Changeset

A test file under `packages/*/src` counts as published source for
`check-changeset-presence`, so the gate demands a changeset — confirmed by running it
before adding one (exit 1). An EMPTY-frontmatter changeset is that gate's own named
exemption and a first-class pass, not a workaround, and it is the honest declaration
here: nothing published moves, because only a comment changed.

## Serial constraint

objectui#9589 is ready and unlanded, and moves two of the mirrors this ratchet
asserts over. Checked at push time: `origin/main` had not moved from the branch point,
so there was nothing to merge and that PR has not landed. The coupling with it is
semantic rather than textual, so if it lands first this branch should be re-merged and
the type-check re-run before review — the ratchet, not the file list, is what would
notice.

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope for this card, filed nowhere by me, recorded here:

- **A stale live figure in this same file, and it is a real one.** A body docblock
  above the ratchet section states that the runtime census reads a `Tests 12 passed`
  line. It reads **32** today. Measured, not guessed: the clean baseline run printed
  `Tests 32 passed (32)`. This is AGENTS.md #9's exact shape — prose that wrote down
  an instrument's answer — and nothing re-derives it. Scope note stated honestly: the
  file header's own "every LIVE figure **in this header** is pinned" claim does not
  formally cover it, because the header docblock closes long before that sentence;
  the contract it does breach is AGENTS.md #9, which is repo-wide. I did **not**
  repair it in place: the neighbouring clause is a RECORD clause that this file's own
  ruling forbids a later card to rewrite, and choosing between deleting the figure and
  pinning it is a judgement, not a mechanical edit. Dedupe words: `zod-mirror-parity`
  · `Tests 12 passed` · stale live figure · runtime census · AGENTS.md #9.
- **Option 3 (splitting the file) is NOT mechanically trivial**, answering the
  ruling's standing question with a reading rather than an opinion. The runtime census
  is not a separable second subject — it exists to pin the type-level half. Below the
  first `describe`, the census references `UnmirroredDeclared` 27 times, `MIRRORS` 19,
  `KnownDrift` 18, `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` 15, `EXPECTED_MIRROR_PAIRS` 12,
  `WiderThanDeclared` 10, `SPEC_DERIVED_PAIRS` 10 and `EXCLUSIONS` 4, and calls
  `readFileSync` 4 times to read source off disk. A split would have to export every
  ledger across a file boundary and keep the census reading the other file's header
  text. Worth recording as evidence against the split being cheap; not worth a card on
  its own.
- The card cited the `include` by a line address, a form AGENTS.md #11 bans in code
  and scripts. It was still accurate when I checked it. Noted only so the next reader
  knows it was verified by content, not trusted. Not filed — issue bodies are not a
  carrier that rule governs, and rewriting a correct card is the more expensive error.

Carrier for the next reader: the three bullets above are for whoever next opens this
file — the first is the only one that should become a card.
